workflows.name: Clean Up a Rough Voice Recording
workflows.description: The repair chain for a recording made in a real room: gate the noise floor, cut the rumble below speech, even out the level, then stop it clipping. Every step is cheap and local — no model involved.

workflows.name: Master a Voice Track
workflows.description: The three-stage chain a voice gets before it ships: compress to even out the peaks, lift the level, then limit so nothing clips. Order matters — limiting first would leave nothing for the compressor.

data.comment:
# 🎙️ Podcast Repurposing Studio

Drop in one episode and ship the whole content pack: titles and show notes, a newsletter edition, five social posts, and quote cards rendered as square images. The episode is transcribed once; four writer branches fan out from the transcript.

**Pipeline:** Episode audio → Transcript → Show notes · Newsletter · Posts · Quotes → Quote cards

**Try this:** pick the ASR, language, and image models, then tune each writer's prompt to your show's voice.

data.prompt:
You are producing the episode page for this podcast.

Show: {{ SHOW }}

From the transcript below, return Markdown, no commentary:

Titles: 3 episode title options — specific, curiosity-driven, under 60 characters.
Summary: one paragraph, 3-4 sentences, written for the episode page.
Show notes: 6-10 bullet chapters in listening order — each a short phrase naming what gets discussed.
Resources: anything mentioned worth linking — books, tools, people, places.
CTA: one closing line using the show's call to action.

Transcript:
{{ TRANSCRIPT }}

data.system: You are a podcast producer who writes episode pages people actually read. Specific and concrete, in the show's voice, no filler.

data.prompt:
Turn this podcast episode into the show's email newsletter edition.

Show: {{ SHOW }}

Return Markdown, no commentary:

Subject: 3 subject-line options under 50 characters.
Body: 150-250 words in the host's voice — open on the episode's single most surprising idea, tease two more takeaways without spoiling them, close with the show's call to action and a listen-link placeholder.

Transcript:
{{ TRANSCRIPT }}

data.system: You write email newsletters for podcasters. Short, personal, in the host's voice — the reader should feel the episode, not a summary of it.

data.prompt:
From this podcast episode transcript, write exactly 5 social posts, one per line — no numbering, no labels, no hashtags unless they earn their place.

Rules:
- Each post stands alone: one idea, claim, or moment from the episode, written to stop the scroll.
- Mix formats across the five: a bold take, a question, a mini-story, a concrete stat or detail, a one-line lesson.
- Plain language in the show's voice ({{ SHOW }}). 280 characters maximum each.

Transcript:
{{ TRANSCRIPT }}

From this transcript, pick exactly {{ COUNT }} verbatim quotes worth putting on a quote card, one per line — no numbering, no attribution, no surrounding quotation marks.

Rules:
- Verbatim from the transcript, lightly trimmed for readability only.
- 8 to 25 words: punchy, self-contained, meaningful without context.
- Prefer strong opinions, hard-won lessons, and vivid phrasing over pleasantries.

Transcript:
{{ TRANSCRIPT }}

Minimal typographic quote card, square 1:1, for this podcast: {{ SHOW }}

Render exactly this text as the centerpiece, large and perfectly legible, spelled exactly as written:
"{{ QUOTE }}"

Clean editorial design: bold modern sans-serif type on a calm, softly textured background, generous margins, one subtle accent color, a small quotation-mark motif. No people, no photos, no logos, no watermark, no words beyond the quote.
